name: Netherlands — Dutch parties
intro: compare it with Dutch political parties
inclusion_note: The test includes the main national parties of Netherlands: those represented in the House of Representatives and those with a significant national following. Positions are the team's estimates and are open to review.
hemicycle_note: Seats in the House of Representatives after the October 2025 general election, arranged left to right. Approximate. 150 members.

SP.name: Socialistische Partij
SP.ideologies: Democratic socialism, Left-wing populism, Soft Euroscepticism
SP.priorities: Public healthcare, Cost of living, Affordable housing, Workers' rights and wages
SP.description: Left-wing populist party that wants a national health fund instead of private insurers, lower rents and higher minimum wages. It is critical of the EU and more cautious on migration than the rest of the left.

PvdD.name: Partij voor de Dieren
PvdD.priorities: Animal welfare, Climate action, Farmers and rural areas
PvdD.description: The world's first animal-rights party to enter a national parliament. It wants to shrink livestock farming, end fossil subsidies and put nature before economic growth.

GL-PvdA.name: GroenLinks–PvdA
GL-PvdA.priorities: Climate action, Affordable housing, Public services, Deeper European integration
GL-PvdA.description: Merged list of the Green Left and the Labour Party, the main force of the Dutch left. It combines climate policy with social security and affordable housing, and strongly supports Ukraine.

Volt.name: Volt Nederland
Volt.priorities: Deeper European integration, Climate action, Digital innovation, Democratic reform
Volt.description: Dutch branch of the pan-European Volt movement. It campaigns for a federal Europe, evidence-based policy and digital and climate transitions.

D66.name: Democraten 66
D66.priorities: Education, Affordable housing, Climate action, Deeper European integration, Democratic reform
D66.description: Social-liberal party that won the most votes in October 2025 under Rob Jetten. Strongly pro-European and progressive on ethical issues, it focuses on education, housing construction and climate.

CDA.name: Christen-Democratisch Appèl
CDA.priorities: Traditional family values, Security and law and order, Affordable housing, Farmers and rural areas
CDA.description: Christian-democratic party that long dominated Dutch politics and recovered strongly in 2025. It stresses community, family, moderate migration policy and a strong EU.

CU.name: ChristenUnie
CU.ideologies: Christian social politics, Christian democracy, Green politics
CU.priorities: Protecting life and family, Traditional family values, Climate action, Minimum income and anti-poverty
CU.description: Protestant Christian party that is socially conservative on euthanasia, drugs and prostitution but centre-left on poverty, refugees and the environment.

VVD.name: Volkspartij voor Vrijheid en Democratie
VVD.priorities: Lower taxes, Reducing immigration, Security and law and order, Fiscal discipline, Nuclear energy
VVD.description: Conservative-liberal party of former prime minister Mark Rutte. It favours low taxes, fiscal discipline, nuclear energy and tighter asylum rules.

BBB.name: BoerBurgerBeweging
BBB.priorities: Farmers and rural areas, Reducing immigration, National sovereignty, Cost of living
BBB.description: Farmer–Citizen Movement, born from protests against nitrogen rules. It defends farmers and rural areas against environmental regulation and 'The Hague' and wants less immigration.

JA21.name: JA21
JA21.ideologies: National conservatism, Economic liberalism, Anti-immigration, Atlanticism
JA21.priorities: Reducing immigration, Security and law and order, Lower taxes, Defence and support for Ukraine
JA21.description: Conservative-liberal party that split from Forum for Democracy. It combines strict immigration policy with free-market economics and a pro-NATO, pro-Ukraine foreign policy.

PVV.name: Partij voor de Vrijheid
PVV.priorities: Reducing immigration, National identity, Cost of living, Public healthcare, National sovereignty
PVV.description: Geert Wilders's party, first in 2023 and tied for first in 2025. It wants an asylum freeze and fewer mosques, combined with left-leaning positions on pensions and healthcare, and is hostile to the EU.

FvD.name: Forum voor Democratie
FvD.leader: Thierry Baudet (Founder), Lidewij de Vos (Party leader)
FvD.priorities: National sovereignty, Direct democracy, National identity, Diplomacy with Russia, no arms deliveries
FvD.description: Hard-right party founded by Thierry Baudet. It wants to leave the EU, rejects most climate policy, was a leading voice against COVID measures and is sympathetic to Russia.
